title: The First Journey Across the Board
summary: A complete 9x9 game taught as a calm journey from the first liberty to a readable final score.

lessons.title: Step onto open ground
lessons.story_hook: Your first stone is a traveler. It needs roads before it needs territory.
lessons.objective: See liberties and choose a first move with room to grow.
remember: Stones live on intersections, not squares.
A liberty is an empty neighboring intersection.
lessons.reflection: After you place a stone, point to every road it can still breathe through.

lessons.title: Stand together without crowding
lessons.story_hook: Two travelers can share strength, but walking shoulder to shoulder is not always the fastest path.
lessons.objective: Connect groups when danger is real and extend when space matters more.
remember: Strength gives you permission to play elsewhere.
lessons.reflection: Did your move add safety, add reach, or merely repeat work already done?

lessons.title: Feel pressure and find the door
lessons.story_hook: When only one road remains, the board is warning you before the capture arrives.
lessons.objective: Recognize atari, escape it, and make an atari without trapping yourself.
remember: Before attacking, count your own liberties too.
lessons.reflection: Which group is most urgent, and how many liberties will it have after your move?

lessons.title: Fight with a purpose
lessons.story_hook: A good fight is not anger. It is a clear exchange: pressure here creates value somewhere.
lessons.objective: Compare capture, connection, escape, and playing elsewhere before choosing a fight.
remember: Urgent moves protect life; big moves build the future.
A threat matters only when ignoring it has a real cost.
lessons.reflection: If the opponent ignores you, what concrete result does your move earn?

lessons.title: Turn presence into a home
lessons.story_hook: Influence is weather, not property. It helps your next action but does not belong to you yet.
lessons.objective: Distinguish strong presence, potential territory, and secure territory.
remember: Influence can attack, defend, or become territory.
Do not count open space as secure too early.
lessons.reflection: Which area is settled, which is only promising, and where can either player still enter?

lessons.title: Finish the story and count
lessons.story_hook: A game ends when both travelers agree there is no valuable road left to take.
lessons.objective: Close the borders, pass responsibly, and read Chinese area scoring.
remember: Under Chinese area scoring, stones and surrounded empty points count.
Two consecutive passes end the game.
lessons.reflection: Can you name the black area, white area, neutral points, komi, and final margin?
